summary: The study reports the deposition of high-quality single-crystal AlN films over sapphire substrates using low pressure metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (LPMOCVD) and switched atomic layer epitaxy (SALE). The SALE process enabled the growth of single-crystal AlN at lower temperatures (as low as 450 “C) compared to conventional LPMOCVD (minimum 750 “C). The crystalline and optical quality of the SALE-grown AlN was comparable to the best LPMOCVD films. The process used TEA and NH3 as precursors with hydrogen as the carrier gas, and the ALE process involved alternating TEA and NH3 pulses.
evidence: The growth process for the low pressure MOCVD of AIN over basal plane sapphire substrates was identical to that used for GaN. Triethylaluminum [TEA) and ammonia ( NH3). were used as the precursors for the depositions. Using the ALE process we were able to deposit single-crystal AIN at temperatures as low as 450 “C. Note for conventional low pressure metalorganic chemical vapor deposited (LPMOCVD) AIN, a minimum growth temperature of 700 “C was required for single-crystal epitaxy. The process we employ for the SALE deposition of AIN is similar to that described earlier for GaN. It closely resembles the procedure used by Dapkus et aI.778 for the deposition of InAs and GaAs. Triethylaluminum (TEA) and ammonia (NH,) were used as precursors with hydrogen as the carrier gas. Similar to GaN ALE6 the sapphire substrate was alternatively subjected to TEA and NH, pulses with the carrier gas on all the time.
